title: Implicit-explicit and split-explicit super-time-stepping methods
summary: Multiphysics initial-value problems couple processes with distinct stability properties, such as advection, diffusion, and stiff local reactions. Standard implicit-explicit (ImEx) additive Runge--Kutta (ARK) methods can treat these processes accurately, but require globally coupled implicit solves when diffusion is grouped with reaction; operator splitting avoids such solves but typically provides weaker coupling and no inexpensive temporal error estimate; and PIROCK is tied to a specific Runge--Kutta--Chebyshev super-time-stepping (STS) construction.
